elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Revised 11.1: "On expiry or termination, Vendor shall provide transition assistance..."; revised 11.2 anchors return to "thirty days after expiry, termination, or Customer's request." The obligations attach to every covered expiry or termination, not only to an anticipated expiry or a request.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: 11.1 as rendered: "Vendor shall provide transition assistance for up to six (6) months." The prior walk-away sentence requiring immediate discontinuation of all assistance is fully replaced, so no contradictory retained text remains.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: 11.1: "...for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates."

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: 11.2 as amended: "Within thirty days after expiry, termination, or Customer's request, Vendor shall return all Customer Data..." The 30-day clock now runs from expiry/termination itself, curing the original request-only trigger; retention of the request trigger is additive and does not weaken the anchor.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: Already met in retained 11.2: "in a complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format, with relationships and metadata reasonably necessary for use." No edit needed.

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: Retained 11.3: deletion occurs "After Customer confirms successful return" and "An authorized officer shall certify deletion in writing." Deletion is sequenced after return, and the former conflicting immediate-deletion language in 11.1 has been removed.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Same operative anchors in revised 11.1 and 11.2 ("On expiry or termination" / "after expiry, termination, or Customer's request").

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: 11.1 provides up to six (6) months of assistance, which exceeds the 90-day fallback floor; the preferred figure is used, so no threshold overshoot beyond the selected (preferred) checklist.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: 11.2 requires return of all Customer Data in machine-readable format within thirty days after expiry or termination.

reasons: Preferred level is complete in operative language: 11.1 supplies the expiry/termination trigger, the six-month assistance period and then-current rates; 11.2 supplies the 30-day return anchored to expiry/termination in a commonly used, documented, machine-readable format; 11.3 supplies certified deletion sequenced after Customer confirms successful return.

The two edits are surgical and necessary. Replacing 11.1 in full was required because its retained words (immediate discontinuation of assistance, permanent deletion, no export or migration support) were walk-away territory and directly contradicted 11.2 and 11.3; adding "expiry, termination, or" to 11.2 was the minimum change to convert a request-only clock into a termination-anchored one.

No extras were added: no survival tail, no at-own-expense language, no procedures, no fee caps or damages categories beyond the checklist. Favourable retained language (no withholding for fee disputes, metadata/relationships, protection of any law-required retained copy, non-use restriction) is preserved verbatim.

Intent is preserved and no dangling references are created: the new six-month period is consistent with 10.1's reference to "any agreed transition period," the request trigger in 11.2 survives as an additional Customer right, and 11.3's confirmation-of-return precondition no longer conflicts with any immediate-deletion mandate.
Fallback is also independently satisfied (six months exceeds 90 days; 30-day export anchored to expiry/termination), so the position is complete at both levels.
